documents.purpose: Minnaert limb-darkening coefficient of Venus's cloud tops at 657 nm from MESSENGER MASCS, red channel.

references.evidence: Perez-Hoyos et al. (2018) fit a Minnaert law to MASCS VIRS spectra of the second Venus flyby (phase 90 +/- 0.5 degrees, zenith angles up to 75 degrees) and plot k against wavelength in Fig. 2. The authors' data file for Fig. 2 (www.ajax.ehu.eus/sph/papers/2017JE005406/fig2_limb_darkening.dat) no longer resolves and the Wayback Machine holds only its listing, so k = 1.346 is read from the published vector figure: the centres of its plotted markers, interpolated linearly to 657 nm.

documents.purpose: Limb halo profile: PSG radiance on limb lines of sight by tangent altitude with the Sun behind the observer, and the nadir radiance under an overhead Sun, in the red (640-670 nm), green (530-560 nm) and blue (440-490 nm) bands. The halo starts at the cloud top, 75 km (Perez-Hoyos et al. 2018).

references.evidence: PSG computes limb and tangential lines of sight with single scattering only (https://psg.gsfc.nasa.gov/images/help/handbook.pdf, p. 96), so these limb calls use NMAX 0 and LMAX 41, the phase-function length PSG asks for the Venus aerosols. PUMAS falls back to a plane-parallel two-stream solver that ignores the tangent altitude when (LMAX+1) x layers x (aerosols+3) x spectral points passes 1e9, so each band is the mean of 5 nm windows, and every answer's method line was checked. With the Sun on the tangent point horizon the single-scattering path is dark, so the Sun sits one degree above it (solar zenith 89 degrees), behind the observer.
references.locator: Handbook chapter 5, section 5 'Specifics of multiple scattering simulations', 'Limb and tangential simulations', p. 96
